passages.original: studium patefacere. Fatendum tamen id scriptum esse, aed apud Arium, cui :opponitur Apostolus. Retorquetur eorum objectio contra ipsos, et vox ingenitus etiam creaturæ communis asseritur. Mox explicato adversariorum ratiocinio, reponit Ambrosius vocibus geniti atque ingeniti non naturam significari, aed qualitatem.
passages.english: to lay open [their] zeal. It must nevertheless be admitted that this is written, but in Arius, to whom the Apostle is opposed. Their objection is turned back against themselves, and the word "unbegotten" is asserted to be common to a creature as well. Then, having set out the reasoning of the opponents, Ambrose replies that by the words "begotten" and "unbegotten" it is not a nature that is signified, but a quality.
passages.notes: This is an editor's summary (argumentum) of the chapter, not Ambrose's own text. The passage begins mid-sentence, so the opening phrase lacks its governing verb. "aed" (twice) is read as "sed" ("but"), and ":opponitur" as "opponitur".

passages.original: 92. Sed si illi d hoc dicunt, quod Arius: justius ego debeo dicere, quod Apostolus dixit (Ephes. III, 14). Patrem enim dixit, non ingenitum nominavit : Filium dixit, et genitum Filium dixit. Quod legi, non nego ; immo libenter usurpo : qnod nOli legi, usurpare non debeo.
passages.english: 92. But if they say this, which Arius [said], I ought with more justice to say what the Apostle said (Eph. 3:14). For he said "Father"; he did not name [him] "unbegotten". He said "Son", and he called the Son "begotten". What I have read, I do not deny; indeed, I gladly make use of it. What I have not read, I ought not to make use of.
passages.notes: The stray "d" after "illi" is taken as a footnote mark and omitted. "qnod nOli" is read as "quod non".
